messages.subject: Obtaining written movement data
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

In the SECR online app under the "Moves" tab it displays a histogram for the distribution of distances between detections and it also displays a summary if the data in text inside a box to the right. The text box includes info such as "Number of moves", Median move", Longest move" etc. I've attached an image so you can see what I mean. I'm wondering how I can get a summary of that movement info within R instead of just the histogram?

I've got the histogram to display fine and this is where I am up to:

> PossumCH <- read.capthist('CHistory_Movements.txt', c("Session1.txt", "Session4.txt", "Session5.txt", "Session6.txt", "Session7.txt"), detector = "multi")
No errors found :-)
> summary(PossumCH, terse = TRUE)
            1 4  5  6  7
Occasions   6 7  8  7  8
Detections 13 3 63 10 51
Animals     9 3 17  5 18
Detectors  10 6 13 14 13
> par(mar = c(1,1,3,1))
> plot (PossumCH, tracks = TRUE)
 1  4  5  6  7
13  3 63 10 51
Warning message:
In plot.capthist(PossumCH, tracks = TRUE) :
  screen layout does not allow for all sessions and some plots may be lost; set par mfrow
> m <- unlist(moves(PossumCH))
> par(mar = c(3.2,4,1,1), mgp = c(2.1,0.6,0))
> hist(m, breaks = seq(-61/2, 500,61), xlab = "Movement m", main = "")

Cheers,

Lachlan

messages.subject: Re: Obtaining written movement data
messages.body_plain:
You seem to be just about there. I don't think there is any single command to provide that summary, but you can assemble the bits:
movementsummary <- function (ch) {
  if (ms(ch)) {
    lapply(ch, movementsummary)
  }
  else {
    m <- moves(ch)
    data.frame(nmoves =  length(unlist(m)),
      median = round(median(unlist(m)),1),
      naiveHNsigma = round(RPSV(ch,CC=TRUE),1),
      longest = round( max(unlist(m)),1))
  }
}
## e.g.
movementsummary(ovenCHp)

But remember there is arbitrariness here in the order of detections on each occasion, so not to be taken too seriously.

messages.subject: Models fitted with fastproximity =F are incompatible
messages.subject_clean: Models fitted with fastproximity =F are incompatible
messages.body_plain:
Dear members,

I am experiencing an issue in the calculation of AIC for a series of models. My data is a multiple occasions capture history, and I have fitted my models using built-in detection covariates (bk and k), topographic detection  covariates, and interactions between built-in parameters and topography. I have also included noneuclidean models using ~bk as detection parameter.
All models, including the null, have been fitted using the argument fastproximity=FALSE. However, the calculation of AIC gives a warning about incompatibility, which is related to the tab data in AICcompatible. Is this related to the detection covariates, and how to fix this eventually?

Thanks to everyone willing to help,

Luciano

messages.subject: Multi-session mixture models with two detector types
messages.subject_clean: Multi-session mixture models with two detector types
messages.body_plain:
Dear Murray,

I'm trying to fit a multi-session (12 sessions) using hcov argument for "Sex", but keep receiving NA's in return. After playing around, I found the problem arises when I add two sessions in which the capture method was foot snares (detector = "single") instead of camera trap (detector = "count") like the other 10 sessions. Out of curiosity, I changed the "detector" of these 2 sessions to see what happens, and, as I expected, the model worked fine when detectors were "count", but returns the same error when I changed them to "multi". Also, instead of using hcov, I tried to add "Sex" as a variable for g0 and sigma, but again I had similar problems in the response (NA's for "esa" values). This error is not a problem with secr's version either, I tried with "4.3.1", "4.3.2", and "4.3.3".

What's the best way of dealing with that?
Sorry if my doubt is too simple, it's the first time I work with secr and after some days of reading and R-coding, I found myself in a dead-end.

I attached the summaries to give a better idea of what I have in hands, as well as the results using "Sex" in the three ways - hcov, g0, and sigma.

I appreciate any insight you could give me.
Many thanks.
Guilherme

messages.subject: Detections in infrared
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

We are conducting a SMR study and about half of our capture events were photographed at night in infrared. We are identifying individuals via colored duct tape on GPS collars. As such, our ability to identify individuals in IR photos is quite different when compared to our day photos. Depending on the season and aid of telemetry, our ability to ID individuals during the day is about 47% to 84% whereas our ability to ID individuals in IR photos is about 3% to 48%. Since our IR photos constitute about half of our data, we would like to keep them in our analysis and account for the difference in our ability to ID between the 2 time periods.

To address this we have split our data into a multi-session model, where we have 1 session for day photos and 1 for night. We therefore have secr.fit(CH, ...pID = ~session, ...). Our data is not independent and therefore, we bootstrapped to acquire larger confidence intervals. That said, we are having issues with the bootstrap producing values that surround our point estimate and are now revisiting our options. Regardless of our bootstrap issue, has anyone else encountered this and have a better method to account for our ability to ID the IR photos?

Our alternative idea is to split each day into 2 occasions, where day 1 = occasion 1, night 1 = occasion 2, etc.

I am also using secr 4.3.3 on Windows OS.

Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Thank you

messages.subject: Habitat Suitability
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I was hoping for some clarity/suggestions with regards to habitat mask and habitat suitability.

I have finished analysing data from a camera trap survey within a fenced protected area (PA). I have run the SECR analysis with 3 different habitat masks. 1st with a hard fence boundary, 2nd with a uniform buffer of 12500m around the trap grid (permeable fence) and lastly a clipped 12500m buffer mask which had certain non-habitat areas removed outside the PA (variable fence permeability).

I was wondering if there is a means of including some sort of habitat suitability variable into the analysis which represents the expected lower habitat quality outside of the PA? I gather this kind of thing has been done my Royle et al. 2013 and Proffitt et al. 2015, using a Resource Selection Function (RSF), but is there a means of doing this in 'secr'?

I should highlight I neither have telemetry data for RSF, nor does the camera trap grid extend outside of the PA.

Any comments or feedback would be greatly valued!

Best,
PJ

messages.subject: Re: Detections in infrared
messages.body_plain:
Can you please be a bit more precise - presumably your call was something like secr.fit(CH, model = list(pID~daynight,...), ...) (pID is not an argument of secr.fit; 'session' has a special meaning in 'secr')? What sort of covariate was your 'session'? What were the issues? Do you really have a case for bootstrapping? messages.body_plain:
I'm sorry but I can't see what is going wrong. When I try to match your problem with one of the builtin datasets everything works fine:

tempCH <- ovenCH
msk <- make.mask(traps(tempCH[[1]]), buffer = 200, nx = 20, type = 'trapbuffer')
# artificially change detector type of two sessions from multi to count
for (i in 3:4) detector(traps(tempCH[[i]])) <- 'count'
fit <- secr.fit(tempCH, mask = msk, hcov = 'Sex', model = g0~h2)
predict(fit)[1:2]

It may be an issue specific to your data. I am sceptical about using 'count' for camera data - the data are so sparse that 'proximity' would be just as good, without raising concerns about independence (if same individual ever recorded twice on one day at one camera). I would also find it tedious to treat every single day (?) as a separate occasion - that slows model fitting for no real benefit. You could at least collapse the count data with 'reduce(by...)' until you get it working. Judging from your use of 'autoini' you have had some trouble with starting values, and that may still be where the problem lies.

Can you see how your data might differ significantly from the ovenbird data? It would help to reproduce the problem with that dataset, or to generate a simpler reproducible example.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Helps in data formats
messages.body_plain:
Those sound like different types of covariate; only 'sex' is potentially a 'group' as the word is used in capture-recapture. 'habitat' sounds like a mask covariate that might be used to model density in 'secr' but not 'openCR' (I infer you are doing an open population analysis as you refer to survival). 'Season' is possibly a session covariate in either package. I suggest you build the model one step at a time, starting with the covariate that is most important to you.

Also, please start a new topic unless your question relates directly to the subject.
